meta.title: The TLS Handshake — Now With the Certificate Check

views.label: 1. The hello
views.note: The browser lists what it can use and asks to speak HTTPS. Day 4 only showed the padlock; now we open it.

views.label: 2. Verify the certificate
views.note: The certificate is a CA's signature binding a public key to the site. Only when that validates against trusted roots does the padlock open.

views.label: 3. Agree a key, go secure
views.note: Asymmetric math lets both sides reach one session key — never sent on the wire. Everything after is symmetric-encrypted.

messages.label: ClientHello  "HTTPS — here are the ciphers I support"
ServerHello + Certificate  "use this cipher; here is my cert"
messages.note: a CA's signature binding a public key to example.com

messages.label: verify  "is this signed by a CA I trust?"
messages.note: the browser checks the signature against its built-in root keys

messages.label: verified  "chain leads to a trusted root — no warning"
agree a session key  "asymmetric math — same key, never sent"
encrypted traffic  "plaintext never touches the wire"
messages.note: the session key now scrambles everything (symmetric)

cards.title: What the padlock now contains
items: ClientHello: the browser lists cipher options and asks for HTTPS
ServerHello + Certificate: a CA-signed claim that this public key belongs to example.com
The check: the signature validates against a trusted root the browser ships with
Then asymmetric math agrees one session key — and all traffic is symmetric-encrypted
